# Glyph

> Glyph is hosted server-driven UI for Android, built on `androidx.compose.remote`. Tenants sign up, push binary `.rc` screen documents from their Gradle build, and Android apps render the updated UI on next launch — natively, no WebView, no JSON schema, no Play Store release.

Glyph (<https://glyph.premex.se>) hosts documents authored against [`androidx.compose.remote`](https://developer.android.com/jetpack/androidx/releases/compose-remote). The Gradle plugin `se.premex.glyph` compiles Compose-like screens to a compact binary format and uploads them via REST; the Android SDK fetches them with ETag revalidation and renders them with the upstream `androidx.compose.remote` player. The same wire format is consumed by iOS (Skia-Metal), Web (Canvas2D), JVM Desktop, and KMP renderers — one `.rc` document, every platform.

Typed accessors are KSP-generated from a server-side manifest that the consumer pins into a `glyph.lock.json` lockfile, so calls like `Glyph.Checkout(userName = "Stefan", totalAmount = 49.99f, callbacks = ...)` are checked at compile time. Host callbacks land via a generated `<Screen>Callbacks` interface; in-document state mutates without a host round-trip.

Free during the `androidx.compose.remote` alpha/beta. Pricing tiers land alongside the upstream framework's GA.

## Documentation

- [Documentation index](https://glyph.premex.se/docs/index.md): map of every doc page below.
- [Getting started](https://glyph.premex.se/docs/getting-started.md): end-to-end walk-through — create an app, configure the Gradle plugin, write a `@RemoteScreen @Composable`, publish, then consume it from a separate Android app with `glyphSync` + generated `Glyph.Foo(...)` accessors.
- [Platforms](https://glyph.premex.se/docs/platforms.md): support matrix and per-platform code samples for Android (shipping), iOS (network + types ship, renderer wiring documented), Web (TypeScript player bundle, used live by the portal), KMP commonMain (JVM target shipping), and JVM Desktop (planned). The shared manifest + `.rc` wire format is identical on every platform.
- [Authoring screens](https://glyph.premex.se/docs/authoring.md): `@RemoteScreen` + `RemoteBox` / `RemoteColumn` / `RemoteRow` / `RemoteText` / `RemoteImage` / `RemoteSpacer` / `RemoteCanvas`, the `RemoteModifier` chain (`fillMaxWidth`, `padding`, `background`, `clickable`, `alpha`), unit literals (`Int.rdp`, `Int.rsp`, `Float.rf`, `String.rs`), typed parameters, click actions, in-document state with `rememberMutableRemoteInt` + `animateRemoteFloat`.
- [Consuming screens](https://glyph.premex.se/docs/consuming.md): pure-consumer Gradle config, `./gradlew :app:glyphSync` to snapshot the server manifest into `glyph.lock.json`, then call the KSP-generated `Glyph.<Screen>(...)` from any `@Composable`.
- [Params and actions](https://glyph.premex.se/docs/params-and-actions.md): typed slot declarations (`RemoteString` / `RemoteFloat` / `RemoteInt` / `RemoteColor`), the `hostAction("name".rs)` factory (replacement for the now-`internal` `HostAction` constructor in alpha11) and how callbacks route through the generated `<Screen>Callbacks` interface, and `valueChange(state, newValue)` for in-document state mutations that bypass the host.
- [Consumer keys](https://glyph.premex.se/docs/consumer-keys.md): opt-in read auth via `X-Consumer-Key: rcc_...`. Difference between the publish key (`rck_`, one per app, used by `glyphPublish`) and consumer keys (`rcc_`, many per app, used by the Android SDK). How to enable `requireConsumerKey`, wire it through `RemoteComposeClient.install(consumerKey = ...)`, and revoke individual keys.
- [REST API reference](https://glyph.premex.se/docs/api-reference.md): every public route (`POST /v1/apps/:appId/screens/:screenId/versions`, `GET /v1/apps/:appId/screens/:screenId.rc`, `GET /v1/apps/:appId/screens/:screenId/preview.png`, `GET /v1/apps/:appId/manifest.json`, `POST /v1/apps/:appId/retention/run`) plus tenant routes (`/v1/me/...`), payload shapes, manifest schema, ETag-based caching behaviour, status codes, and a live `curl` example against the demo tenant.

## Blog

- [Remote Compose is portable UI, and the server is just one boundary it crosses](https://glyph.premex.se/blog/remote-compose-portable-ui): A Remote Compose document is a portable description of drawing, not a screen tied to one origin. The same bytes cross a process, a display, or the network.
- [Remote Compose gives you a format, not a pipeline](https://glyph.premex.se/blog/remote-compose-publishing-pipeline): The alpha hands you an authoring DSL and a capture call. Turning that into versioned bytes a device can fetch is a pipeline you build yourself.
- [A2UI and Remote Compose: two ways an agent can draw a native Android screen](https://glyph.premex.se/blog/a2ui-and-remote-compose): Agents are starting to emit UI as JSON intent. On Android, how does that render natively? A2UI and Remote Compose solve different halves of the problem.
- [Remote Compose is now the widget engine. That changes server-driven UI.](https://glyph.premex.se/blog/remote-compose-is-the-widget-engine): Google I/O 2026 framed Remote Compose as the rendering engine behind Jetpack Glance, replacing RemoteViews and ProtoLayout. What that means if you've been using it for server-driven UI.
- [After the Remote Compose roundtrip: what you reach for next](https://glyph.premex.se/blog/after-the-remote-compose-roundtrip): Author bytes on the JVM, render them on Android. Once the writer roundtrip works, the next questions are delivery, cache, fallback, and type safety.
- [What happens to your screens if Remote Compose gets deprecated?](https://glyph.premex.se/blog/what-happens-if-remote-compose-gets-deprecated): Android has a long deprecation history, and Remote Compose is a new format from the same vendor. Worth thinking through the worst case before betting a roadmap on it.
- [Which screens belong on the server? A decision framework for Remote Compose adoption](https://glyph.premex.se/blog/which-screens-belong-on-the-server): Five axes — change frequency, latency, offline, security, audit — that decide whether a screen should ship over the wire or stay in your APK.
- [Server-driven UI vs server-driven code: why Remote Compose ships drawing ops, not Kotlin](https://glyph.premex.se/blog/rc-vs-ktx-bundles): Three wire formats for Android server-driven UI — JSON, Kotlin bytecode, and Remote Compose drawing ops. Why format determines what you can ship.
- [What is Remote Compose? Server-driven UI for Android, native and small](https://glyph.premex.se/blog/what-is-remote-compose): Remote Compose is an AndroidX framework that lets a server send a screen to your app as a few kilobytes of binary, rendered natively by Compose. How it works and how to use it.
- [Remote Compose vs WebView vs JSON-driven UI: when each one wins](https://glyph.premex.se/blog/remote-compose-vs-webview): Server-driven UI on Android in three flavours — WebView, JSON-driven Compose, and Remote Compose. An honest comparison and when to reach for each.
- [Type-safe server-driven UI: contracts, lockfiles, and KSP-generated accessors](https://glyph.premex.se/blog/type-safe-server-driven-ui): Server-driven UI is fragile when consumers consume by string. How to make Remote Compose screens type-safe end to end with contracts, lockfiles, and a KSP code generator.
- [The .rc binary format: how Remote Compose ships UI in kilobytes](https://glyph.premex.se/blog/rc-binary-format): Remote Compose serialises Compose drawing operations into a compact binary stream. What the bytes look like, how to read them, and why it ends up so small.
- [Updating Android UI without a Play Store release: a Remote Compose playbook](https://glyph.premex.se/blog/updating-ui-without-app-updates): How to ship UI changes without the Play Store safely — caching strategy, ETag revalidation, rollback, A/B testing, and offline fallback.
